text:
mina: Heads up — DSAR deletion for user 0xA failed to finish; pipeline errored during keystore access after last night's RBAC sweep. Anyone seen this? :thinking:
security-bot: Alert: service-account 'dsar-deleter' denied cloudkms:Decrypt at 2026-03-20T23:12Z (error=PERMISSION_DENIED)
alex: I saw the same in the job logs — hitting permission denied when the deleter hits the keystore proxy. RBAC tightener rolled yesterday removed a broad infra SA grant.
samir: Confirmed, I rolled a policy to remove wide `serviceAccountAdmin` bindings. It looks like `dsar-deleter` lost `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt`.
jess: Don't re-grant broadly. Legal needs deletion proof. We can do a short-lived exception to finish pending deletes, but it must be logged and scoped.
alex: If we grant a temporary exception, ensure `data_access` audit logs are exported and we snapshot the deletion manifests. Also tag logs with the DSAR case id so legal can find them.
legal-team: We need: object ids attempted, deletion timestamps, who triggered, and the final deletion proof (manifest + keystore audit). Please record chain-of-custody.
samir: I'll craft a narrow policy that allows `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` only from `serviceAccount:dsar-deleter@infra` and only for resource `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/embeddings/cryptoKeys/primary`. Will also enable Data Access audit logs for that resource.
mina: Note — some orphaned snapshots in eu-west-1 were referenced by the index and may require a separate purge path; the delete job hits both the DB manifest and S3 snapshots.
jess: Two asks: (1) get approval for a 24h retention-exception window to complete backlog; (2) make any keystore change audit-only for the window (no permanent role grants).
alex: I'll canary the policy in staging and run a DSAR replay against a staging subset. Plan: PR with explicit `resourceNames` + `condition` limiting invocations to the DSAR pipeline id.
security-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-1198 — DSAR deletion blocked by RBAC change. Assignees: samir, alex, jess. Status: triage.
legal-team: If exception is granted, append `retention_exception_case: DSAR-1756` to all audit exports and CC legal@redwood on the proof bundle. Also freeze related exports for 48h pending review.
samir: Policy PR: https://git.internal/repos/infra/policies/12345 — applying in ~10m. Keeping previous role in a temp allowlist for `dsar-deleter` only.
mina: After PR deploys I'll re-run the deletion job and post receipts.
alex: Deletions succeeded. Proof bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-privacy-proofs/DSAR-1756/proof-bundle.tar.gz (manifests + cloudaudit slices + keystore access logs).
legal-team: Received the bundle. We'll validate and close if everything matches. Please retain the policy change and audit history for 90 days for compliance.
jess: Follow-up action: add a pre-check to the DSAR pipeline that verifies keystore permissions (fast `iam.testIamPermissions` + audit export presence) and fails fast with a retention-exception form link.
mina: Good call. Also recommend adding a small smoke test that runs a dry-delete on a sandbox key to detect RBAC regressions before production runs.
alex: I pushed a pipeline change and a smoke test PR: https://git.internal/repos/infra/dsar-smoketests/9 — will monitor for 24h.
security-bot: Incident #INC-2026-1198 updated: status -> resolved, resolution -> temporary-scoped-policy-applied + proofs archived.
